clue.text: Opted to have many pairs of stockings

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, so it stands for many
hose is an old collective word for stockings or tights

explanation.surface: Someone decided to own a large collection of stockings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Many' gives C, the Roman hundred, a standard crossword convention; 'to have' only links it to the hosiery.
explanation.definitionFit: To have opted is to have made a choice, the past tense of select.

clue.text: Damage caused by one member who is overbearing

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
MP is a Member of Parliament
split as over bearing: in this down clue the member sits over AIR, a bearing or manner

explanation.surface: Harm done by a domineering committee member.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overbearing' looks like bossiness, but read as 'over bearing' it places MP above AIR (bearing, demeanour) in the down entry; 'who is' merely links.
explanation.definitionFit: To damage something is to weaken or spoil it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Detectives examination provides conclusive proof

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'Detectives examination provides conclusive proof' gives CID + TEST but nothing for the leading A; a word (likely 'A') seems lost in OCR and no source found

clue.text: Study by doctor needs to be notedly brisk

parts.note: to con is an old verb meaning to study or learn by heart
MO is a Medical Officer, an army doctor
taken as written

explanation.surface: A doctor's research must be carried out with speed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Notedly' signals a musical direction: in a score the Italian phrase asks the player to go with movement.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian tempo marking, meaning with motion, tells players in written music to keep a lively pace.

clue.text: The type to give an impudent look

definitions.meaning: a heavy printing typeface used for emphasis
a cheeky, brazen expression worn by someone shameless

explanation.surface: A certain kind of person tends to stare at others insolently.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both a heavy printed font and, as a phrase, a brazen countenance worn by the shameless.

clue.text: George offers gold to self-righteous crew

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
taken as written
pi is slang short for pious, so sanctimonious
a lot is a group or crew of people

explanation.surface: A man named George hands treasure to a sanctimonious gang.
explanation.walkthrough: George was RAF slang for an aircraft's automatic flight control, so the name is the definition, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Airmen nicknamed the automatic steering system of an aircraft George, a slang synonym.

clue.text: Fool about to add bitter flavouring some meat

parts.note: a chump is a fool or idiot
C is short for circa, Latin for about
the hop flavours bitter, the British beer

explanation.surface: An idiot sets out to season a cut of meat with something bitter.
explanation.walkthrough: Bitter is a British style of beer, flavoured with hops; C (circa) for 'about' is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a thick cut taken from the chump end of a loin of lamb, a kind of butcher's cut.

clue.text: Lily means a great deal to you and me

parts.note: a lot means a great deal
us is the pronoun for you and me together

explanation.surface: This flower matters enormously to the two of us.
explanation.definitionFit: The sacred water plant of Egypt and Asia is commonly called a water lily, so this is an example.

clue.text: What the bibliophile may reserve

parts.note: a ... lover's object of affection, and also a verb meaning to make a reservation, as at a library

explanation.surface: A book collector puts something aside for later.
explanation.definitionFit: A bibliophile loves volumes, and to reserve a table or seat is to make a booking.

clue.text: Mother chases a bird on the Nile

indicators.note: to chase is to follow behind, so the mother comes after the bird

parts.note: taken as written
a swan is a large water bird
a dam is the mother of an animal, especially a horse

explanation.surface: A mother animal pursues a bird along the Nile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bird' and 'Mother' tempt you toward a nesting picture, but the definition is the place: 'on the Nile' names a structure on that river.
explanation.definitionFit: The great barrage at Aswan, in southern Egypt, is built across the river, so it stands on it.

clue.text: Not even a patient man can get casual work

parts.note: an odd number is not even
Job, in the Bible, is proverbial for his patience

explanation.surface: An uneven-tempered patient person finds occasional employment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The patience of Job' is proverbial, so 'patient man' points to the biblical figure, not someone in hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: Occasional small tasks done for pay are casual work, a phrase synonym.

clue.text: Quite right to place junction at top of French road

indicators.note: placing one thing at the top of another sets it in front, at the start

parts.note: a T-junction is shaped like a T
rue is French for street or road

explanation.surface: Correct to put a crossroads at the start of a road in France.
explanation.definitionFit: Something accurate or correct is said to be so, an adjective synonym.

clue.text: Heed advice to accept a gratuity

definitions.meaning: to follow a hint or suggestion someone gives
to take a small extra payment for service, as a waiter does

explanation.surface: A waiter listens to counsel and pockets a bit of money.
explanation.walkthrough: The grid prints TAKEADIP, but both senses need TIP: a hint, and a gratuity.
explanation.definitionFit: A tip is both a piece of advice and a small gift of money, so taking one fits both readings.

clue.text: A dishonest dealer catches influenza despite wealth

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: to catch is to take in, so the dealer holds the illness inside

parts.note: a fence is a dealer in stolen goods
flu is short for influenza

explanation.surface: A crook comes down with the flu in spite of being rich.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Catches' is the container signal; 'despite' is only a loose link before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Riches and prosperity are what this abstract noun names, a synonym.

clue.text: Not working in the Tax Office to start with

indicators.note: this phrase puts the office part first, ahead of the tax

parts.note: off. is an abbreviation of office
a duty is a tax, as on imports

explanation.surface: Someone at the tax office is on a break before the day begins.
explanation.walkthrough: OFF. is a standard abbreviation of 'office'; 'to start with' puts it in front of DUTY.
explanation.definitionFit: An employee who is between shifts and free is not at work.

clue.text: When upset Edward longed to be aloof

indicators.note: in a down entry, upset turns the name upside down, so it reads bottom to top

parts.note: Ted is a pet form of the name Edward
to ache for is to long for

explanation.surface: A man named Edward was hurt and yearned to keep his distance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' turns TED to read DET in this down entry; 'When' and 'to be' only link.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone distant and uninvolved is emotionally separate, a synonym.

clue.text: Billy Bunter became a spiv

definitions.meaning: the fat schoolboy of the Greyfriars stories, broad in the girth
a flashy small-time crook dealing in black-market goods

explanation.surface: A famous fictional schoolboy grew up to be a petty crook.
explanation.walkthrough: Billy Bunter is the greedy, very fat pupil in Frank Richards' British school stories; a spiv is a British word for a sharp black-market dealer.
explanation.definitionFit: Bunter is literally a broad lad, while the phrase is British slang for a shady wheeler-dealer.

clue.text: Wantonly disregard refining process

indicators.note: to process material is to work it over, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Purifying methods are being recklessly ignored.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Process' is the anagram signal for REFINING.
explanation.definitionFit: To breach a rule or a right is to violate it without regard.

clue.text: Game archdeacon confronts one boy

parts.note: Ven., the Venerable, is the title of an archdeacon
I is the Roman numeral for one
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: A senior cleric faces up to a lone lad.
explanation.walkthrough: An Anglican archdeacon is styled 'the Venerable', abbreviated VEN; 'confronts' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: Deer meat is a kind of game, the term for hunted animals eaten as food.

clue.text: Standard charge for an apartment

definitions.meaning: a single fixed price applying to everyone
read literally, the cost of renting a dwelling on one floor

explanation.surface: The usual fee for renting a dwelling.
explanation.definitionFit: A uniform fee for everyone; and, literally, what a British apartment costs.

clue.text: Italian banker receives a Royal Navy cipher

parts.note: taken as written
a cipher is a zero, the figure O

explanation.surface: A banker in Italy gets a secret code from the navy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banker' is a crossword term for a river, which has banks; 'cipher' means zero, not a code.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the river flowing through Florence and Pisa, something with banks.

clue.text: Commotion in one of Corfu's streets

indicators.note: in shows the letters sit inside the words Corfu's streets

explanation.surface: A disturbance broke out in a street on a Greek island.
explanation.definitionFit: A noisy to-do or bother is a commotion, a synonym.

clue.text: Look around very fast

indicators.note: around means the look surrounds the other letter

parts.note: to stare is to look fixedly

explanation.surface: Glance about very quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast' is the verb (go without food), not 'quick'.
explanation.definitionFit: To go hungry or go without food is the verb sense of fast.

clue.text: Medium has to have resources

definitions.meaning: a channel or method by which something is done
money or wealth to live on

explanation.surface: A spiritualist needs money.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both a method or channel and one's wealth, as in a man of substance.

clue.text: Signal from a firm in Scottish highland

indicators.note: in puts the article and firm inside the mountain

parts.note: a ben is a Scottish mountain, as in Ben Nevis
taken as written
Co. is short for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A message comes from a company based up in the Scottish hills.
explanation.walkthrough: BEN is the Scots word for a mountain peak, as in Ben Nevis.
explanation.definitionFit: A hilltop fire or light used to warn or guide is a signal.

clue.text: Reproduced a diet Tim worked out

indicators.note: worked out suggests the letters are exercised into a new order

explanation.surface: A man named Tim copied a meal plan he had devised.
explanation.definitionFit: To copy or mimic something is to reproduce it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Fix an uncomplimentary prison warder

definitions.meaning: to fasten with a threaded fastener
slang, mildly rude, for a jail guard

explanation.surface: Repair a disrespectful jail guard.
explanation.definitionFit: It means to fasten something tight, and is British prison slang for a guard.

clue.text: In favour of being generous and compassionate

parts.note: for means in favour of
a giving person is generous

explanation.surface: Supporting kindness and mercy.
explanation.definitionFit: A merciful, pardoning nature shows compassion, a synonym.
